use_when:
Buttons communicate actions that people can take. They are typically placed throughout the UI, in places like: Dialogs, Modal windows, Forms, Cards, Toolbars
They can also be placed within standard button groups.
Use visually-prominent filled buttons for the most important actions
A button container’s width is dynamically set to fit its label text
Button container width can be responsive, which allows it to stretch horizontally

dont_use_when.text: Don’t clutter your UI with too many buttons. Consider presenting low-priority actions in overflow menus or as icon buttons.
dont_use_when.alternative: overflow menus or as icon buttons

dont_use_when.text: A button container’s width shouldn’t be narrower than its label text
Don’t wrap text. For maximum legibility, label text should remain on a single line.

best_practice: Use sentence case for button label text, capitalizing the first word and proper nouns
Buttons can move in the layout, but elements should remain in the same order

a11y.text: Renders a native <button> element with no role attribute.
type defaults to "button", so it does not submit a surrounding form.
state="disabled" sets the native disabled attribute.
onClick does not fire while state="disabled".
In the tab order (tabIndex 0) with no tabindex attribute set.
Does not call preventDefault on keydown; a consumer onKeyDown handler receives the event.
Native button attributes pass through, including aria-label.
:focus-visible draws an outline of var(--border-width-focused) solid var(--color-border-focused), offset var(--border-width-default).
prefers-reduced-motion: reduce removes the background and border transition.
